match.reason: No bank point teaches atom economy or the green chemistry idea; the closest, chem-yield-purity, covers percentage yield and purity but not atom economy, so it is related rather than the same point.

draft.title: Atom economy and yield
card: compares the mass of product actually collected with the mass the equation says is possible. % yield = actual mass ÷ theoretical mass × 100. It is lowered by incomplete reactions, side reactions and losses during separation.

compares the mass of the desired product with the total mass of all reactants in the balanced equation. Atom economy = molar mass of desired product ÷ total molar mass of reactants × 100, using the coefficients.
Yield depends on how well the reaction is carried out. Atom economy depends only on the equation, so a reaction can have a 100% yield and a low atom economy if it makes a lot of by-product.
favours a high atom economy, because more of the reactant atoms end up in the product and less becomes waste. An addition reaction that makes only one product has an atom economy of 100%.
draft.remember: Yield shows how well a reaction was carried out. Atom economy shows how much of the reactants the equation turns into product.

a.q: Which change would raise the percentage yield of a reaction without changing its equation?
opts: Losing less product when it is separated
Choosing a reaction with fewer by-products in its equation
Using a different balanced equation for the same product
Dividing by the total molar mass of reactants
a.why: Percentage yield compares the mass actually collected with the theoretical mass, so less loss during separation raises it. Changing the equation changes the atom economy, not how well a given reaction is carried out.
a.clue: Yield is about what happens in the flask and afterwards, not what is written in the equation.

b.q: Reaction X makes ethanol in 100% yield, but the equation also produces a large mass of waste by-product. What is true of reaction X?
opts: Its atom economy is low, though its yield is high
Its atom economy is high, because its yield is high
Its atom economy is 100%, because no product is lost
Its yield is low, because a by-product forms
b.why: Atom economy depends on the equation. A large by-product means less of the reactant mass ends up in ethanol, so atom economy is low. A 100% yield only shows that all the possible ethanol was collected, so it does not make the atom economy high.
b.clue: Which measure depends only on the balanced equation, and which on the amount collected?

a.best: Losing less product when it is separated

b.best: Its atom economy is low, though its yield is high
